name: Standalone Upstream-Compatible BF16 Paged GQA Decode Portable CUDA From-Zero Lab v2

work.agent_query:
Read AGENT_TASK.md and README_AGENT.md before changing code. Starting from the empty submission, implement the exact seven-argument BF16 paged-GQA decode ABI with self-contained Triton, correct and memory-safe over the whole declared support domain (any batch 1-256, any S_q 1-16, any GQA group size with H_q <= 128, a power of two or not, page sizes 1-256, page tables wider than needed, page pools larger than B x width with shared pages, cache lengths up to 1,048,576, and cache slots no query may see holding NaN or Inf), computing only in BF16 and FP32; then optimize the decode, speculative, long-context and sequence families across the whole support domain. Your score comes from hidden test cases on the Judge, which differ from the public tests and can be much larger; the public tests are for getting the kernel working. Your final result is the best valid score you reach within the time budget, so keep versioned candidates and leave FINAL_VERSION on your strongest clean candidate. Check candidates with the public edge and sanitizer suites (tools/run_public_tests.sh --edge or --sanitize with --candidate-version N) before submitting, and before finishing run the full public suite, the edge suite and the sanitizer suite once on the selected version:

```bash
tools/run_public_tests.sh --candidate-version N
tools/run_public_tests.sh --edge --candidate-version N
tools/run_public_tests.sh --sanitize --candidate-version N
```

Evaluate candidates only by the feedback from the public tests and your submissions; existing implementations and attention kernels may not be used in the submission, and Judge internals are unavailable. Before each manual submission, wait for all public-test and compiler workers to exit, then run sforge-submit --details; each Judge run takes part of your budget.

decode.workload: one decode step of a serving engine rank: trace-derived uneven lengths, shared prefix pages, fragmented pool, wide table

spec.workload: draft-token verification at small batch sizes

stream.workload: 512 consecutive decode steps of one server; compilation during timed steps counts

support_domain.gqa: h_q % h_kv == 0, any group size, query head h reads kv head h // (h_q / h_kv)
support_domain.page_table: int32 [b, width], width >= ceil(l_max / page_size), contiguous
support_domain.page_pool: any size >= the pages used; page ids in [0, pool) and may repeat (shared prefix pages)
support_domain.unspecified_contents: table entries past ceil(l_b / page_size) are valid page ids; cache slots j >= l_b and unused pages may hold any BF16 bit pattern, NaN and Inf included

invariants: bottom-right causal decode over the realized per-request cache length through the int32 page table

support domain: any 1<=B<=256, any 1<=S_q<=16, h_q<=128 with any group size h_q/h_kv, page sizes 1-256 (powers of two), cache lengths up to 1,048,576, page tables wider than needed, page pools larger than B x width with repeated page ids
the output depends only on visible keys: hidden cache slots, unused pages and unused table entries may hold any value, NaN and Inf included
BF16 inputs and output, computation in BF16 and FP32 only, within the kvcache tolerance rule (max error <= 2x, mean error <= 1.5x of a BF16 reordered reference, plus the 5e-3 normalized-L2 backstop)
the output is fully written on the current stream, nothing outside out and the call's own scratch is written, and every input is unchanged
host code obeys the statically checked subset: no host loops, comprehensions, default arguments, tensor math or device queries; kernels are @triton.jit / @triton.autotune only
no existing attention or GEMM kernel, compiled extension, private stream, replay, dynamic loading, evaluator introspection or shape-specific shortcut
the 168 private edge cases (12 also under compute-sanitizer memcheck, run first) are zero-weight hard gates that never enter the score

spec.case_statistic: median_trial_tflops for single calls; total work over total step time for streams
